questions.title: DeLong variance and normal interval for one empirical ROC AUC
questions.description: Focused integrated L0 known-result evaluation grounded in DeLong, DeLong, and Clarke-Pearson (1988), Sun and Xu (2014), and pinned pROC v1.19.1 source. Let X_1,...,X_m be independent case scores and Y_1,...,Y_n independent control scores, with the two samples independent and larger scores indicating cases. Use h(x,y)=1{x>y}+0.5*1{x=y} and theta=E h(X,Y)=P(X>Y)+0.5 P(X=Y). In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX workspace, derive the empirical AUC as a two-sample U-statistic, its unbiasedness, case and control structural components, the exact finite-sample variance decomposition including the order-1/(mn) degenerate contribution, and the two-sample projection CLT when m/(m+n) tends to lambda in (0,1). Derive the DeLong leading variance estimator from sample variances of the placements, state assumptions sufficient for consistency and normal inference, and distinguish that asymptotic standard-error estimator from exact finite-sample variance or exact coverage. Establish the population AUC Phi((mu_X-mu_Y)/sqrt(sigma_X^2+sigma_Y^2)) for independent Gaussian scores, including the equal-variance reduction. Treat ties explicitly and state the limits of clipping a normal interval to [0,1]. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_delong_auc and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. It may use NumPy or SciPy but must not call a prebuilt ROC-AUC, DeLong, ranking, or confidence-interval routine. Exploratory Python or R may compare direct pairwise and midrank calculations and inspect special cases. A separately frozen confirmatory experiment uses predeclared continuous Gaussian and tie-heavy ordinal designs, independent exact formula checks, AUC bias, standard-error calibration, and normal-interval coverage with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Such computation supports only the frozen designs and is not proof. Source-code replication and novelty are not required, and Lean formalization is not applicable.

primary_paper.title: Comparing the Areas under Two or More Correlated Receiver Operating Characteristic Curves: A Nonparametric Approach

algorithm_paper.title: Fast Implementation of DeLong's Algorithm for Comparing the Areas Under Correlated Receiver Operating Characteristic Curves

implementation_convention.title: pROC DeLong placements and single-AUC confidence interval
implementation_convention.meaning: The model-visible excerpts fix the tie-aware structural-component and variance conventions; the public estimator contract below is executable authority.

request_fields.name: case_scores
request_fields.meaning: Independent scalar scores from the case population; a larger score indicates stronger evidence for case status.
request_fields.indexing: input order is observational only and has no inferential meaning
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nested values, nonfinite values, and fewer than two scores; preserve ties and do not coerce entries.

request_fields.name: control_scores
request_fields.meaning: Independent scalar scores from the control population on the same scale and direction as case_scores.
request_fields.indexing: input order is observational only and has no inferential meaning
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nested values, nonfinite values, and fewer than two scores; preserve ties and do not coerce entries.

request_fields.name: confidence_level
request_fields.meaning: The two-sided normal-interval confidence level fixed before observing this request.
request_fields.shape: one finite scalar strictly between zero and one
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonfinite values, zero, one, and values outside (0,1); do not silently replace or round the level.

response_fields.name: n_cases
response_fields.meaning: The number m of supplied case scores.
response_fields.shape: one native integer at least two
response_fields.edge_cases: Must not count omitted or padded scores.

response_fields.name: n_controls
response_fields.meaning: The number n of supplied control scores.
response_fields.shape: one native integer at least two
response_fields.edge_cases: Must not count omitted or padded scores.

response_fields.name: confidence_level
response_fields.meaning: The exact confidence level supplied in the request.

response_fields.name: auc
response_fields.meaning: The empirical tie-aware ROC area theta_hat.
response_fields.indexing: averages every case-control pair exactly once
response_fields.edge_cases: Use half credit for exact ties and do not reverse the declared score direction.

response_fields.name: case_placements
response_fields.meaning: The structural component V10_i for each case in original input order.
response_fields.edge_cases: Each entry averages h(case_scores[i],control_scores[j]) over all n controls with half credit for ties.

response_fields.name: control_placements
response_fields.meaning: The structural component V01_j for each control in original input order.
response_fields.edge_cases: Each entry averages h(case_scores[i],control_scores[j]) over all m cases with half credit for ties.

response_fields.name: case_component_variance
response_fields.meaning: The unbiased sample variance of the m case placements.

response_fields.name: control_component_variance
response_fields.meaning: The unbiased sample variance of the n control placements.

response_fields.name: auc_variance
response_fields.meaning: The DeLong leading variance estimate for auc.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not pool placements or add a pairwise Bernoulli variance term.

response_fields.name: standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The nonnegative square root of auc_variance.
response_fields.edge_cases: May be zero when all placements are equal.

response_fields.name: ci_lower
response_fields.meaning: The lower endpoint of the clipped two-sided normal interval.

response_fields.name: ci_upper
response_fields.meaning: The upper endpoint of the clipped two-sided normal interval.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly case_scores, control_scores, and confidence_level, and the response contains exactly the twelve declared fields. Missing, extra, malformed, coercible-only, or nonfinite values are rejected.
The mean of case_placements and the mean of control_placements both equal auc up to floating-point tolerance, with exact half credit for ties.

The two component variances use divisors m-1 and n-1, auc_variance equals case_component_variance/m plus control_component_variance/n, and standard_error squared equals auc_variance up to floating-point tolerance.
Applying the same positive affine score transformation a*s+b with a>0 to cases and controls leaves all returned quantities except the unchanged counts and confidence level numerically unchanged.
Permuting either input sample leaves every scalar output unchanged; the corresponding placement array changes only by the same permutation.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen input, all candidate outputs agree with an independent direct pairwise implementation and the public transformations under predeclared numerical tolerances.
Across predeclared independent Gaussian and tie-heavy ordinal designs, mean estimated AUC is compared with an independently computed population AUC and Monte Carlo uncertainty.
Across the frozen designs, the average DeLong standard error is compared with the empirical sampling standard deviation of auc.
The frozen assessment records clipped normal-interval coverage and its Monte Carlo standard error; it does not require exact finite-sample nominal coverage.
Finite source checks and simulations are computational evidence only; they do not prove U-statistic asymptotics, DeLong consistency, or validity for arbitrary score distributions.
